disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of any offense involving moral turpitude
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of any offense involving moral turpitude, in which case the record of conviction or a certified copy thereof certified by the clerk of the court or by the judge in which court the conviction is had shall be conclusive evidence of such conviction.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Unprofessional conduct including fraud, fee splitting, fraudulent advertising, and unauthorized use of drugs
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Unprofessional conduct including any conduct of a character likely to deceive or defraud the public, lending his or her license to any person, the employment of "cappers," or "steerers" to obtain business, "splitting" or dividing a fee with any person or persons

disciplinary_grounds.description: Obtaining a license or certificate by fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Obtaining a license or certificate by fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation, whether knowingly or unknowingly practiced on the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Suffering from a contagious or infectious disease
disciplinary_grounds.quote: When the holder of a license or certificate is suffering from a contagious or infectious disease.

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Intemperance in the use of intoxicating liquors or narcotics to such an extent as to unfit the holder of the license for the proper practice of podiatry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to renew license and pay any prescribed penalty

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Sexual misconduct including, but not limited to, any or all of the following: a. Engaging in or soliciting a consensual or nonconsensual sexual relationship when a podiatrist-patient relationship exists.

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any other misconduct defined by the board.

definition_quote.value: The diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the human foot and ankle, as described herein.
definition_quote.quote: PODIATRY. The diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the human foot and ankle, as described herein.

methods_authorized.quote: The diagnosis and medical or surgical or mechanical or manipulative or electrical treatment of any ailment of the human foot or ankle and the surgical treatment of ailments of the human foot or ankle limited anatomically to the foot or ankle.

drug_authority.value: A podiatrist may prescribe drugs that relate specifically to the scope of practice authorized herein.
drug_authority.quote: A podiatrist may prescribe drugs that relate specifically to the scope of practice authorized herein.

anatomical_scope_upper_boundary.quote: the surgical treatment of ailments of the human foot or ankle limited anatomically to the foot or ankle

amputation_authorized.quote: The practice of podiatry shall include the amputation of the toes and other parts of the foot and ankle, but shall not include any amputation above the Chopart joint

anesthesia_authority.quote: shall not include ... the administration of any anesthetic other than local

ankle_surgery_authorized.quote: A podiatrist may not surgically treat osseous ailments of the ankle unless he or she has completed at least 36 months of post-graduate residency training approved by the Council on Podiatric Medical Education of the American Podiatric Medical Association.

ankle_surgery_residency_requirement.quote: A podiatrist may not surgically treat osseous ailments of the ankle unless he or she has completed at least 36 months of post-graduate residency training approved by the Council on Podiatric Medical Education of the American Podiatric Medical Association.

systemic_disease_treatment_excluded.quote: The term does not include the medical treatment of any systemic disease, but includes treatment for the local manifestations of those systemic diseases in the foot or ankle.

systemic_disease_local_manifestations_in.quote: The term does not include the medical treatment of any systemic disease, but includes treatment for the local manifestations of those systemic diseases in the foot or ankle.
